findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] add a proving step showing that after the guard withdraws tools the agent actually emits a `completion_verdict` (e.g. reuse the tool-free finalizer path), so the 'lands a verdict' AC is exercised, not just the detection trigger
evidence: 'the already-shipped tool-withdrawal actuator is triggered, so the agent lands a completion_verdict on the evidence gathered'
Testing lists trace-replay tests that fire the guard; none demonstrates that withdrawal actually results in an emitted verdict
findings.finding: The AC 'the agent lands a completion_verdict ... instead of being killed' asserts an LLM-dependent outcome (the agent emits a verdict once tools are withdrawn), but the listed proving commands are all offline replays of recorded traces that exercise the DETECTION/withdrawal, not the actual verdict-emission after withdrawal.
scenarios: Guard fires and withdraws tools, but the agent still fails to emit a verdict (e.g. the tool-free finalizer path is not reached the same way), leaving the runaway still killed

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] define the window (24) and threshold (0.50) as named, single-source constants and capture the runaway-detection design decision in an ADR / AGENTS.md note
evidence: 'distinct(last 24 tool calls) <= 0.50 fires on all three pathological runs'
no mention of exposing window/threshold as a named constant or documenting the new guard's design decision
findings.finding: The discriminator constants (window=24, threshold<=0.50) are asserted as hardcoded values derived from four runs; the plan does not state whether they are named/configurable constants, and a novel detection stage wired into the tool-filter predicate is introduced with no ADR/AGENTS.md note.
findings.location: 'The discriminator that works: a windowed distinct-ratio'
scenarios: Model behavior shifts and the 0.50/24 tuning needs adjustment; hardcoded literals buried in the predicate are hard to find and re-tune

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] bound the per-invocation cost of the discriminator to the trailing window (do not re-derive signatures over the entire growing history on every tool-filter call)
evidence: 'usage_log.failure_usage duck-types on a plain message list ... so the existing signature logic runs verbatim on the live history'
the predicate at agent_call.py:64-73 is invoked per tool call
findings.finding: The guard recomputes distinct-ratio by running failure_usage signature logic over the live message history on every tool-filter invocation, i.e. per model request across a growing history, which trends toward O(n^2) over a full run of 250+ requests.
scenarios: A long healthy run (258+ requests) re-walks the entire message history each request just to look at the trailing 24-call window

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how a tools-withdrawn turn on the structured verify step is made to emit a schema-valid completion_verdict (e.g. inject a finalize instruction on withdrawal, or route to the shipped tool-free finalizer), so 'lands a verdict' is a mechanism, not an assumption.
evidence: Plan: 'Withdraw tools when a runaway is detected, so the agent lands a verdict on the evidence it has.'
completion-verification.yaml:40-43 — verify step is `mode: structured` / `output_schema: completion_verdict` (a schema-constrained turn, not free text)
agent_call.py:70-75 — the filter only makes tools UNAVAILABLE; it does not inject any instruction telling the model to finalize a verdict

The shipped precedent (completion_recovery.py:509-521) lands a verdict via a SEPARATE tool-free `single_turn` FINALIZER call with explicit finalizer instructions — not by silently withdrawing tools from the primary agentic step
findings.finding: The mechanism assumes that withdrawing tools mid-run forces the agent to emit a valid completion_verdict, but does not establish that a structured-output agentic step (mode: structured, output_schema: completion_verdict) produces a schema-valid verdict on a tools-withdrawn turn rather than re-requesting tools or emitting prose that fails structured validation (a non-verdict error of its own).
scenarios: Runaway trips the guard at call 88; tools vanish; the model's next turn still tries to call a (now-filtered) tool or emits an explanation instead of a verdict, so the structured contract validation raises and the step still dies with no verdict.
findings.suggested_fix: State that on runaway detection the step routes to the already-shipped tool-free structured finalizer path (completion_recovery.py finalizer), or that tool withdrawal is paired with a finalize directive, and add an AC/test asserting the withdrawn-tools turn produces a schema-valid completion_verdict rather than a validation error.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Address why a verdict landed on the runaway's own (looping) history is trustworthy to SIGN, or route the landing through clean/isolated evidence (as the shipped recovery finalizer does) rather than the poisoned primary context.
evidence: Plan (withdrawn-plan rationale): landing early yields 'a worse verdict, not a safer one, and on a gate that SIGNS its output'

The chosen fix lands the verdict on the SAME history that just looped (e.g. SPLIT-A's 144x repeated identical search) rather than on the clean isolated-criteria evidence the shipped recovery path assembles (completion_recovery.py:453-486)
The signed verdict flows to sign_completion_verdict (transition_close.py:171) — attestation quality matters
findings.finding: The plan does not address that landing a verdict on the runaway's own primary history means the signed verdict is produced from the context in which the agent demonstrably looped — the same 'worse verdict on deliberately-degraded evidence, on a gate that SIGNS its output' objection the plan raises to defeat the flat-landing alternative applies to landing-on-loop and is left unanswered.
scenarios: SPLIT-A trips the guard at call 88 after 144 identical no-progress calls; the verdict is landed and signed on a poisoned/confused history, attesting completion on evidence the agent itself could not resolve.
findings.suggested_fix: Either justify that the accumulated pre-loop evidence in the primary history is sufficient to sign, or specify that runaway detection hands off to the isolated-criteria recovery + tool-free finalizer (which already gathers clean per-criterion evidence) so the signed verdict is not built from the looping context.

This ticket does not restate the concrete field/accessor its actuator will read from the repetition summary, so the decision rule is not co-located with the schema (the summary dict) that must supply it.

findings.suggested_fix: State the concrete summary key the actuator consumes and require 70bc to expose that exact field/semantics (window-configurable, order-insensitive set cardinality) so the two tickets share one named contract.

agent_call.py:64-73 (verified) only filters toolsets to unavailable; it has no mechanism to force an emission
The existing UnretryableOutputError/token-exhaustion recovery (completion_recovery.py:429-432) is gated on token exhaustion, a different condition than post-withdrawal non-emission
